030/**
031 * Printf-style string formatter with a small cache and lenient argument handling.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * This class provides a thread-safe, cacheable formatter for printf-style ({@link java.util.Formatter}) patterns
035 * (<js>"%s"</js>, <js>"%d"</js>, <js>"%.2f"</js>, <js>"%1$s"</js>, etc.). MessageFormat-style (<js>"{0}"</js>)
036 * patterns are <b>not</b> recognized here — <c>{</c> and <c>'</c> are treated as literal text. For MessageFormat
037 * rendering use {@link StringUtils#mformat(String, Object...)} / {@code Shorts.mf(...)}/{@code Shorts.mfs(...)}
038 * (backed by {@link java.text.MessageFormat}).
039 *
040 * <h5 class='section'>Features:</h5>
041 * <ul>
042 *   <li><b>Printf grammar:</b> <js>"%s"</js>, <js>"%d"</js>, <js>"%.2f"</js>, <js>"%1$s"</js>, etc.</li>
043 *   <li><b>Thread-Safe:</b> Immutable class, safe for concurrent use</li>
044 *   <li><b>Cacheable:</b> Use {@link #ofPrintf(String)} for cached instances</li>
045 *   <li><b>Lenient null handling:</b> <jk>null</jk> arguments render as <js>"null"</js> for string conversions
046 *       (rather than throwing) and a fast path avoids {@link java.util.Formatter} for simple <js>"%s"</js> tokens</li>
047 * </ul>
048 *
049 * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
050 * <p class='bjava'>
051 *    <jc>// Simple printf</jc>
052 *    StringFormat <jv>fmt</jv> = StringFormat.<jsm>ofPrintf</jsm>(<js>"Hello %s, you have %d items"</js>);
053 *    String <jv>result</jv> = <jv>fmt</jv>.<jsm>format</jsm>(<js>"John"</js>, 5);
054 *    <jc>// Returns: "Hello John, you have 5 items"</jc>
055 *
056 *    <jc>// Argument index (reuse arguments)</jc>
057 *    StringFormat <jv>fmt2</jv> = StringFormat.<jsm>ofPrintf</jsm>(<js>"%1$s loves %2$s, and %1$s also loves %3$s"</js>);
058 *    String <jv>result2</jv> = <jv>fmt2</jv>.<jsm>format</jsm>(<js>"Alice"</js>, <js>"Bob"</js>, <js>"Charlie"</js>);
059 *    <jc>// Returns: "Alice loves Bob, and Alice also loves Charlie"</jc>
060 * </p>
061 *
062 * <h5 class='section'>Caching:</h5>
063 * <p>
064 * Use {@link #ofPrintf(String)} to get cached instances. The cache is thread-safe and limited to 1000 entries.
065 * For uncached instances, use the constructor directly.
066 * </p>
067 *
068 * <h5 class='section'>Thread Safety:</h5>
069 * <p>
070 * This class is immutable and thread-safe. Multiple threads can safely use the same instance concurrently.
071 * </p>
072 *
073 * @see StringUtils#format(String, Object...)
074 * @see StringUtils#mformat(String, Object...)
075 */
076@SuppressWarnings({
077   "java:S115" // Constants use UPPER_snakeCase convention
078})
079public final class StringFormat {
080
081   // Argument name constants for assertArgNotNull
082   private static final String ARG_pattern = "pattern";
083
084   /**
085    * Literal text token.
086    */
087   private static final class LiteralToken extends Token {
088      private final String text;
089
090      LiteralToken(String text) {
091         this.text = text;
092      }
093
094      @Override
095      public String toString() {
096         return "[L:" + text + "]";
097      }
098
099      @Override
100      void append(StringBuilder sb, Object[] args, Locale locale) {
101         sb.append(text);
102      }
103   }
104
105   /**
106    * Printf-style token (e.g., %s, %d, %.2f).
107    */
108   private static final class StringFormatToken extends Token {
109      private final char format; // 's' = simple (handle directly), 'o' = other (use String.format)
110      private final String content; // The format string to pass to String.format (null for simple formats)
111      private final int index; // 0-based index
112
113   StringFormatToken(String content, int index) {
114      // content is everything after '%' (e.g., "s", "1$s", "d", ".2f", "1$.2f")
115      var dollarIndex = content.indexOf('$');
116      if (dollarIndex >= 0) {
117         index = parseIndex(content.substring(0, dollarIndex)) - 1;
118         content = content.substring(dollarIndex + 1);
119      }
120         this.format = content.length() == 1 ? content.charAt(content.length() - 1) : 'z';
121         this.index = index;
122         this.content = "%" + content;
123      }
124
125      /**
126       * Parses the index from a StringFormat content string.
127       *
128       * @param s The content string (e.g., "1", "2").
129       * @return The parsed index.
130       */
131      private static int parseIndex(String s) {
132         return Integer.parseInt(s);
133      }
134
135      /**
136       * Creates a StringFormatToken and adds it to the tokens list.
137       *
138       * @param tokens The list of tokens to add to.
139       * @param pattern The pattern string.
140       * @param start The start index in the pattern.
141       * @param end The end index in the pattern.
142       * @param index The token index.
143       */
144      static void create(List<Token> tokens, String pattern, int start, int end, int index) {
145         tokens.add(new StringFormatToken(pattern.substring(start, end), index));
146      }
147
148      @Override
149      public String toString() {
150         return "[S:" + format + index + ":" + content + "]";
151      }
152
153      @Override
154      @SuppressWarnings({
155         "java:S3776", // Cognitive complexity acceptable for this specific logic
156         "java:S6541", // StringBuilder used in local scope; no synchronization needed
157      })
158      void append(StringBuilder sb, Object[] args, Locale locale) {
159         // String.format() throws MissingFormatArgumentException when argument is missing
160         if (args == null || index >= args.length || index < 0) {
161            throw new MissingFormatArgumentException(content);
162         }
163         var o = args[index];
164         var l = locale == null ? Locale.getDefault() : locale;
165         var dl = locale == null || locale.equals(Locale.getDefault());
166         switch (format) {
167            case 'b':
168               // String.format() with %b converts:
169               // - null -> "false"
170               // - Boolean -> toString()
171               // - Any other non-null value -> "true"
172               if (o == null) {
173                  sb.append("false");
174               } else if (o instanceof Boolean) {
175                  sb.append(o.toString());
176               } else {
177                  sb.append("true");
178               }
179               return;
180            case 'B':
181               // String.format() with %B converts:
182               // - null -> "FALSE"
183               // - Boolean -> toString().toUpperCase()
184               // - Any other non-null value -> "TRUE"
185               if (o == null) {
186                  sb.append("FALSE");
187               } else if (o instanceof Boolean) {
188                  sb.append(o.toString().toUpperCase());
189               } else {
190                  sb.append("TRUE");
191               }
192               return;
193            case 's':
194               if (o == null) {
195                  sb.append("null");
196                  return;
197               }
198               sb.append(o.toString());
199               return;
200            case 'S':
201               if (o == null) {
202                  sb.append("NULL");
203                  return;
204               }
205               sb.append(o.toString().toUpperCase());
206               return;
207            case 'd':
208               if (o == null) {
209                  sb.append("null");
210                  return;
211               }
212               if (o instanceof Number o2) {
213                  if (dl) {
214                     if (o instanceof Integer || o instanceof Long || o instanceof Byte || o instanceof Short) {
215                        sb.append(o);
216                     } else {
217                        // For other Number types (BigDecimal, BigInteger, etc.), convert to long
218                        sb.append(o2.longValue());
219                     }
220                     return;
221                  }
222                  // For non-default locales, use String.format to ensure printf-style consistency
223                  sb.append(sf(l, "%d", o));
224                  return;
225               }
226               break;
227            case 'x':
228               if (o == null) {
229                  sb.append("null");
230                  return;
231               }
232               if (o instanceof Integer o2) {
233                  sb.append(Integer.toHexString(o2));
234                  return;
235               } else if (o instanceof Long o2) {
236                  sb.append(Long.toHexString(o2));
237                  return;
238               }
239               break;
240            case 'X':
241               if (o == null) {
242                  sb.append("NULL");
243                  return;
244               }
245               if (o instanceof Integer o2) {
246                  sb.append(Integer.toHexString(o2).toUpperCase());
247                  return;
248               } else if (o instanceof Long o2) {
249                  sb.append(Long.toHexString(o2).toUpperCase());
250                  return;
251               }
252               break;
253            case 'o':
254               if (o == null) {
255                  sb.append("null");
256                  return;
257               }
258               if (o instanceof Integer o2) {
259                  sb.append(Integer.toOctalString(o2));
260                  return;
261               } else if (o instanceof Long o2) {
262                  sb.append(Long.toOctalString(o2));
263                  return;
264               }
265               break;
266            case 'c':
267               if (o == null) {
268                  sb.append("null");
269                  return;
270               }
271               if (o instanceof Character) {
272                  sb.append(o);
273                  return;
274               } else if (o instanceof Integer o2) {
275                  sb.append((char)o2.intValue());
276                  return;
277               }
278               break;
279            case 'C':
280               if (o == null) {
281                  sb.append("NULL");
282                  return;
283               }
284               if (o instanceof Character o2) {
285                  sb.append(Character.toUpperCase(o2));
286                  return;
287               } else if (o instanceof Integer o2) {
288                  sb.append(Character.toUpperCase((char)o2.intValue()));
289                  return;
290               }
291               break;
292            case 'f':
293               if (o == null) {
294                  sb.append("null");
295                  return;
296               }
297               // Always use String.format() to match exact behavior (precision, etc.)
298               if (o instanceof Number) {
299                  sb.append(sf(l, "%f", o));
300                  return;
301               }
302               break;
303            default:
304               break;
305         }
306
307         // Fallback to String.format for any other simple format
308         sb.append(sf(l, content, o));
309      }
310   }
311
312   /**
313    * Base class for format tokens.
314    */
315   private abstract static class Token {
316
317      /**
318       * Appends the formatted content to the StringBuilder.
319       *
320       * @param sb The StringBuilder to append to.
321       * @param args The arguments array.
322       * @param locale The locale for formatting (can be null for default).
323       */
324      abstract void append(StringBuilder sb, Object[] args, Locale locale);
325   }
326
327   private static final CacheMode CACHE_MODE = env("juneau.StringFormat.caching", CacheMode.FULL);
328
329   private static final Cache<String,StringFormat> CACHE = Cache.of(String.class, StringFormat.class).maxSize(1000).cacheMode(CACHE_MODE).build();
330
331   private static final AsciiSet PRINTF_CONVERSION_CHARS = AsciiSet.of("bBhHsScCdoxXeEfgGaAtTn%");
332
333   private static final AsciiSet PRINTF_FORMAT_CHARS = AsciiSet.of("-+ 0(#.*$");
334
335   /**
336    * Formats a pattern string with the given arguments using printf-style semantics.
337    *
338    * <p>
339    * <c>{</c> and <c>'</c> are literal text, matching {@link java.util.Formatter} semantics.
340    * If no arguments are passed in, the pattern is returned as-is.
341    *
342    * @param pattern The format pattern.
343    * @param args The arguments to format.
344    * @return The formatted string.
345    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the pattern is <jk>null</jk> or format specifiers are invalid.
346    */
347   public static String formatPrintf(String pattern, Object...args) {
348      if (args.length == 0)
349         return pattern;
350      return ofPrintf(pattern).format(args);
351   }
352
353   /**
354    * Formats a pattern string with the given arguments using printf-style semantics and the specified locale.
355    *
356    * @param pattern The format pattern.
357    * @param locale The locale to use for formatting. If <jk>null</jk>, uses the default locale.
358    * @param args The arguments to format.
359    * @return The formatted string.
360    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the pattern is <jk>null</jk> or format specifiers are invalid.
361    */
362   public static String formatPrintf(String pattern, Locale locale, Object...args) {
363      if (args.length == 0)
364         return pattern;
365      return ofPrintf(pattern).format(locale, args);
366   }
367
368   /**
369    * Returns a cached printf StringFormat instance for the given pattern.
370    *
371    * <p>
372    * This method uses a thread-safe cache to avoid recreating StringFormat instances for the same pattern.
373    * The cache is limited to 1000 entries. <c>{</c> and <c>'</c> are treated as literal text (genuine
374    * {@link java.util.Formatter} semantics); only printf-style placeholders are recognized.
375    *
376    * @param pattern The format pattern.
377    * @return A cached or new StringFormat instance.
378    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the pattern is <jk>null</jk>.
379    */
380   public static StringFormat ofPrintf(String pattern) {
381      assertArgNotNull(ARG_pattern, pattern);
382      return CACHE.get(pattern, () -> new StringFormat(pattern));
383   }
384
385   private static void lit(List<Token> tokens, String pattern, int start) {
386      if (start == pattern.length())
387         return;
388      tokens.add(new LiteralToken(pattern.substring(start)));
389   }
390
391   private static void lit(List<Token> tokens, String pattern, int start, int end) {
392      if (start == end)
393         return;
394      tokens.add(new LiteralToken(pattern.substring(start, end)));
395   }
396
397   /**
398    * Parses the pattern into a list of tokens.
399    */
400   @SuppressWarnings({
401      "java:S125", // S125: state-machine/docs comments
402      "java:S3776", // Cognitive complexity acceptable for this specific logic
403      "java:S6541", // Single-threaded context; synchronization unnecessary
404      "java:S1871" // else-branch intentionally duplicates known-conversion branch; semantics differ (valid vs unknown format char)
405   })
406   private static List<Token> parseTokens(String pattern) {
407      var tokens = new ArrayList<Token>();
408      var length = pattern.length();
409      var i = 0;
410      var sequentialIndex = 0; // 0-based index for sequential placeholders
411
412      // Possible String.format variable formats:
413      // %[argument_index$][flags][width][.precision]conversion
414      // %[argument_index$][flags][width]conversion
415      // %[flags][width]conversion
416
417      // S1 - In literal, looking for %
418      // S2 - Found %, looking for conversion char or t or T
419      var state = S1;
420
421      var mark = 0;
422      while (i < length) {
423         var ch = pattern.charAt(i++);
424
425         if (state == S1) {
426            if (ch == '%') {
427               lit(tokens, pattern, mark, i - 1);
428               state = S2;
429               mark = i;
430            }
431         } else /* if (state == S2) */ {
432            if (ch == '%') {
433               tokens.add(new LiteralToken("%"));
434               state = S1;
435               mark = i;
436            } else if (ch == 'n') {
437               // %n is special - it doesn't consume an argument, so handle it as a literal token
438               tokens.add(new LiteralToken(System.lineSeparator()));
439               state = S1;
440               mark = i;
441            } else if (ch == 't' || ch == 'T') {
442               // Do nothing.  Part of 2-character time conversion.
443            } else if (PRINTF_CONVERSION_CHARS.contains(ch)) {
444               StringFormatToken.create(tokens, pattern, mark, i, sequentialIndex++);
445               state = S1;
446               mark = i;
447            } else if (PRINTF_FORMAT_CHARS.contains(ch) || Character.isDigit(ch)) {
448               // Do nothing.
449            } else {
450               // Unknown character - could be invalid conversion or end of format
451               // Create StringFormatToken and let String.format() validate it
452               // This allows String.format() to throw IllegalFormatException for invalid conversions like %F
453               // printfStart is position after '%', so substring from printfStart-1 (the '%') to i (after the char)
454               StringFormatToken.create(tokens, pattern, mark, i, sequentialIndex++);
455               state = S1;
456               mark = i;
457            }
458         }
459      }
460
461      // Process remaining content based on final state
462      if (state == S1) {
463         lit(tokens, pattern, mark);
464      } else /* if (state == S2) */ {
465         // Dangling '%' without conversion - throw exception to match String.format() behavior
466         // UnknownFormatConversionException constructor takes just the conversion character
467         throw new UnknownFormatConversionException("%");
468      }
469
470      return tokens;
471   }
472
473
474   @SuppressWarnings({
475      "java:S3398" // sf() is a generic String.format wrapper; keeping it at outer-class scope alongside other utility methods is intentional
476   })
477   private static String sf(Locale l, String s, Object o) {
478      return String.format(l, s, a(o));
479   }
480
481   private final String pattern;
482
483   private final Token[] tokens;
484
485   /**
486    * Creates a new printf StringFormat instance.
487    *
488    * <p>
489    * <c>{</c> and <c>'</c> are treated as literal text (genuine {@link java.util.Formatter} semantics); only
490    * printf-style placeholders are recognized.
491    *
492    * @param pattern The format pattern.
493    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the pattern is <jk>null</jk>.
494    */
495   public StringFormat(String pattern) {
496      this.pattern = assertArgNotNull(ARG_pattern, pattern);
497      this.tokens = parseTokens(pattern).toArray(Token[]::new);
498   }
499
500   @Override
501   public boolean equals(Object o) {
502      return o instanceof StringFormat o2 && eq(this, o2, (x, y) -> eq(x.pattern, y.pattern));
503   }
504
505   /**
506    * Formats the pattern with the given arguments using the specified locale.
507    *
508    * <p>
509    * The locale affects locale-specific printf number formatting (decimal separators, etc.).
510    *
511    * @param locale The locale to use for formatting. If <jk>null</jk>, uses the default locale.
512    * @param args The arguments to format.
513    * @return The formatted string.
514    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If format specifiers are invalid or arguments don't match.
515    */
516   public String format(Locale locale, Object...args) {
517      var sb = new StringBuilder(pattern.length() + 64);
518      for (var token : tokens) {
519         token.append(sb, args, locale);
520      }
521      return sb.toString();
522   }
523
524   /**
525    * Formats the pattern with the given arguments using the default locale.
526    *
527    * @param args The arguments to format.
528    * @return The formatted string.
529    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If format specifiers are invalid or arguments don't match.
530    */
531   public String format(Object...args) {
532      return format(Locale.getDefault(), args);
533   }
534
535   @Override
536   public int hashCode() {
537      return pattern.hashCode();
538   }
539
540   /**
541    * Returns a debug representation of the parsed pattern showing the token structure.
542    *
543    * <p>
544    * This method is useful for debugging and understanding how a pattern was parsed.
545    * It returns a string showing each token in the format:
546    * <ul>
547    *   <li><b>Literal tokens:</b> <js>"[L:text]"</js> - Literal text</li>
548    *   <li><b>StringFormat tokens (simple):</b> <js>"[S:s0:%s]"</js> - Simple printf placeholder (format='s', index=0, content)</li>
549    *   <li><b>StringFormat tokens (complex):</b> <js>"[S:z0:%.2f]"</js> - Complex printf placeholder (format='z', index=0, content)</li>
550    * </ul>
551    *
552    * <h5 class='section'>Token Format:</h5>
553    * <ul>
554    *   <li><b>L</b> = Literal token</li>
555    *   <li><b>S</b> = StringFormat (printf) token</li>
556    *   <li><b>Format character:</b> 's' = simple, 'z' = complex printf</li>
557    *   <li><b>Index:</b> 0-based argument index</li>
558    *   <li><b>Content:</b> The format string content (for complex tokens)</li>
559    * </ul>
560    *
561    * <h5 class='section'>Examples:</h5>
562    * <p class='bjava'>
563    *    StringFormat <jv>fmt</jv> = StringFormat.<jsm>ofPrintf</jsm>(<js>"Hello %s, you have %d items"</js>);
564    *    <jv>fmt</jv>.<jsm>toPattern</jsm>();
565    *    <jc>// Returns: "[L:Hello ][S:s0:%s][L:, you have ][S:d1:%d][L: items]"</jc>
566    * </p>
567    *
568    * @return A debug string showing the parsed token structure.
569    */
570   public String toPattern() {
571      return Arrays.stream(tokens).map(Object::toString).collect(Collectors.joining());
572   }
573
574   @Override
575   public String toString() {
576      return pattern;
577   }
578}
